thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: High latency detected on canary cluster 'us-east-canary-1' for model-serving endpoints (p95 > 1.5s). Triggered 2026-04-12T09:12:03Z. Pager notifying on-call.
Maya L.: I'm on pager. Saw deployment rl-20260412-03 finished ~3m prior. Canary traffic at 25%.
Rahul P.: That rollout used runtime image runtime:v2.4.0-beta. New kernel selector was enabled by default: feature runtime.kernel_auto_select=on.
Jin T.: Checking canary node logs now. Seeing repeated messages about falling back from fused_attention kernel to scalar kernel.
Jin T.: log excerpt:
```
[09:10:50] kernel_selector: attempting fused_attention_v3
[09:10:50] kernel_selector: fallback -> scalar_attention (reason: unsupported_unaligned_stride)
[09:10:51] kvcache: warmup miss rate 42%
[09:10:51] batching: queue length spike -> 18
[09:10:52] perf: p95 increased 0.3s -> 1.8s
```
Maya L.: Could the quantized kernel path be incompatible with some model sharding? We onboarded a new attention tiling logic in this image.
Rahul P.: Looks like the selector picks fused kernels aggressively for long-seq requests, but for a subset of request shapes it can't handle misaligned tiles and falls back to slow path. Also observed a bunch of requeues: batching-worker logs show requests requeued due to processing-time overshoot.
Ops-bot: Detected surge in batching latency and increased CPU on host canary-3. Auto-scaling attempted to add instance but failed health checks during cold start.
Maya L.: Two quick actions: 1) disable kernel_auto_select on canary, 2) throttle max_batch_tokens. Can someone flip flag and lower batch size?
Rahul P.: Disabling flag now: `redctl feature set runtime.kernel_auto_select=false --scope=canary --immediate`
incident-bot: Feature toggle accepted (id ft-3092). Monitoring metrics.
Jin T.: After toggle (90s), kernel fallback logs dropped by 90%, kv-cache miss rate down to ~9%, but p95 still ~1.1s (improved but not baseline). We still see some requeues for very large payloads.
Maya L.: Lowering batching threshold: `PATCH /config/runtime/canary-1 { "batching.max_batch_tokens": 400 }` returned 200. Reloading config.
Ops-bot: Config reload applied; warnings: some inflight requests may be requeued.
Jin T.: Immediate effect: batch sizes reduced, but throughput decreased slightly. Latency p95 trending down to 0.6s after 3 minutes.
Maya L.: Given partial recovery, I'm going to roll back the canary image to runtime:v2.3.4 (last stable). Initiating rollback: `deploy rollback --cluster=canary --to=rl-20260410-88` at 09:19:32Z.
incident-bot: Rollback started. Health checks being evaluated.
Rahul P.: Rollback completed on canary at 09:22:10Z. New kernels not present; kernel selector back to stable logic. p95 now 0.38s across canary.
support-bot: Initial customer impact: estimated 4.5% of prod API calls routed through canary window experienced elevated p95 >1s between 09:12-09:22. Logged customer tickets CT-9123 and CT-9124 from two enterprise accounts reporting slow responses. Creating incident INC-2401 and linking tickets.
Maya L.: Putting an org-wide hold on rollout rl-20260412-03: `release-control freeze --id=rl-20260412-03 --reason='kernel selector causing regressions'`.
Rahul P.: Creating follow-up issues: RUNTIME-502: harden kernel selector for unaligned strides; RUNTIME-503: add synthetic canary test for long-context unaligned attention patterns; OPER-221: ensure control plane autoscaling handles cold starts during canary.
Jin T.: Notes for postmortem: 1) kernel selector lacked compatibility check for specific tiling; 2) canary tests didn't include larger-context traces; 3) feature flags applied in rollout allowed unsafe selector default on. We'll propose add gate that requires explicit opt-in per model until selector proves compatibility.
Maya L.: Handoff to on-call follow-up: I'll monitor metrics for 45m, coordinate customer comms with support, and own the postmortem. Rahul, Jin - you own the fixes.
support-bot: Draft customer communication created in INC-2401. Suggested copy: brief incident summary, mitigation actions (rollback, config fixes), and contact for follow-up. Waiting approval from Maya L.
Ops-bot: Alert cleared on canary at 09:24:00Z after rollback and config changes. No further paging for this incident.
Maya L.: Thanks team. Postmortem scheduled for tomorrow 11:00 PT. Closing thread; will update INC-2401 with logs and timeline.
Rahul P.: :thumbsup:
Jin T.: :white_check_mark:
